items.headline: New York sues Kalshi, will seek damages, alleging it offers gambling platform
items.subheadline: The state is seeking a penalty equal to three times Kalshi’s gains from the activity, plus $100,000 for each unauthorized or attempted offer of sports or mobile sports wagering,.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: U.S. sanctions Iran-linked bitcoin insurance scheme for Strait of Hormuz ships
items.subheadline: The Treasury Department said the Hormuz Safe platform accepted bitcoin and other digital assets as part of an alleged sanctions workaround tied to IRGC-backed shipping controls.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: The systemic-risk debate over perpetual futures is aimed at the wrong target
items.subheadline: As perpetuals enter regulated markets, critics warn they import systemic risk. But the risk comes from venue design — leverage limits, margin rules, index construction, and default handling — not the contract itself, argues Chris Tyrer, President of Bullish Exchange.
items.author: Chris Tyrer

items.headline: Everything is becoming a perp
items.subheadline: The perpetual — the 24/7, leveraged contract that crypto invented and then perfected — is no longer just a way to trade crypto, says Katana Network’s Matthew Fisher. It’s becoming the way to trade everything.
items.author: Matthew Fisher

items.headline: RWA perps will outpace tokenization
items.subheadline: Tokenization was crypto's first big export to TradFi. Perps are next, says Martin Lee, markets insight lead at DWF labs.
items.author: Martin Lee

items.headline: Everyone has the perps convergence backwards
items.subheadline: Crypto is said to be growing up to look like Wall Street. The evidence in its biggest market points the other way, argues Bitget CEO Gracy Chen.
items.author: Gracy Chen

items.headline: Iran-linked crypto network moved $4B through Dubai exchange
items.subheadline: Blockchain investigators traced billions in crypto through Shelbit, with hundreds of millions later reaching Binance and other major crypto exchanges.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Coinbase's (COIN) weak quarter leaves Wall Street split on timing of a recovery
items.subheadline: Most analysts blamed a weak crypto market for Coinbase's earnings miss, though opinions diverged on when trading activity will recover.
items.author: Helene Braun

items.headline: Circle secures New York trust charter as crypto regulatory push accelerates
items.subheadline: The approval lets the USDC issuer offer fiduciary and custody services under New York banking law.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Coinbase wants to be Canada’s ‘everything exchange,’ but says clearer rules are needed first
items.subheadline: Coinbase Canada's new CEO, Eric Richmond, says permanent rules, rather than temporary exemptions, are needed as the company pushes to expand into derivatives, tokenized assets and decentralized finance.
items.author: Aoyon Ashraf

items.headline: The UK has finally shown it’s serious about crypto
items.subheadline: Several recent regulatory steps indicate the UK might finally stop dragging its feet when it comes to crypto, argues Wirex CEO Chet Shah.
items.author: Chet Shah

items.headline: About $80 million ZEC crosses into Zcash's Ironwood pool in the first day
items.subheadline: Roughly 5% of the funds in the retired Orchard pool have gone through the turnstile. The rest sit in a pool that can no longer take deposits.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: BTC, ETH price news: Bitcoin at $64,000 as Kospi's record 17% surge leaves crypto untouched
items.subheadline: Samsung and SK Hynix both jumped more than 23%. Bitcoin moved a fraction of a percent in the past 24 hours, and most majors are still lower on the week.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Brale bets new protocol can solve stablecoin liquidity bottleneck
items.subheadline: Today's bridge model won't scale as hundreds of companies issue their own stablecoins, fragmenting liquidity, Brale CEO Ben Milne said in an interview.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Crypto exchange Luno cuts 20% of staff amid automation push and retail trading slumps
items.subheadline: The DCG-owned company previously cut 35% of staff in January 2023 citing tough market conditions.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Scammers stole millions of XRP tokens from dozens of investors via a fake Flare Network site
items.subheadline: Investors were tricked into believing they would receive over 1.5% yields monthly were robbed of at least $8.5 millon worth of XRP.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Ondo Finance explores deal valued at up to $500 million
items.subheadline: The tokenized-assets firm is considering an acquisition valued at $250 million to $500 million as consolidation accelerates across crypto infrastructure.
items.author: Will Canny

items.headline: JPMorgan, Citi, UBS test tokenized cross-border payments in BIS pilot
items.subheadline: Twenty-eight banks, including JPMorgan, Citi and UBS, moved real money across borders in a live test of blockchain-based settlement.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Quantum Solutions, Hyperscale Data tap crypto treasuries to fund AI data centers
items.subheadline: The firm’s board raised the sale cap to 4,375 ETH through Oct. 30, nearly 66% of June holdings, although 3,050 of its remaining ETH is pledged.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Bitcoin mining difficulty shrinks 14% from this year's high as plunging revenues force operators to pivot
items.subheadline: Difficulty falls as weak mining economics reduce capacity, while forward markets signal little relief through year-end.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Live updates: 'Worst hit in Bitcoin history' – longtime Bitcoiners react to Coincard flaw
items.subheadline: The Bank of Japan left its benchmark at 1% and Governor Ueda's hawkish signals landed softly, since markets had already priced an October hike.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Bitcoin (BTC) is as hard to trade right now as it was in January
items.subheadline: Bitcoin is as hard to trade now as in January. A standard deviation study shows its daily price swings at their tightest in six months, with volatility collapsing into small ranges. Here's what could happen next.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: Bitcoin slides on the final day of July while equities boom
items.subheadline: The BTC price fell as July drew to a close, even as stocks gained in Asia and U.S. index futures advanced. The CoinDesk 20 (CD20) index is set to post its biggest gain since July 2025.
items.author: Oliver Knight

items.headline: 2026 FIFA World Cup saw $20 billion in prediction market volume
items.subheadline: Markets ranged from the simple question of who would win the tournament to whether Cristiano Ronaldo would cry when Portugal were eliminated (he did).
items.author: Jamie Crawley

items.headline: Ethereum (ETH) news: Foundation names pcaversaccio to board amid leadership changes
items.subheadline: pcaversaccio (known as "pc"), is a prominent security researcher in the Ethereum ecosystem. His addition brings the foundation's board to four members.
items.author: Margaux Nijkerk

items.headline: As crypto perpetual futures boom, Ethereum’s role is shifting
items.subheadline: Rather than competing directly with faster chains, some builders argue Ethereum's strength lies in supporting the layer-2 networks where trading is taking place.
items.author: Margaux Nijkerk

items.headline: Bitcoin's quantum plan assumes some algorithms break. AI just weakened one in 60 hours
items.subheadline: The HAWK system isn't deployed anywhere, and Bitcoin doesn't use it. But is sitting in the same quantum race that Bitcoin developers are scrambling to finish.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Live updates: Bitcoin holds above $64,000 as Nasdaq surges on AI trade comeback
items.subheadline: The Nasdaq gained more than 2%, with Microsoft higher by 15% after its cloud unit grew at the fastest pace in four years while it held the line on spending.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Ethereum enters its second decade after a year of upheaval at the foundation
items.subheadline: Few periods in Ethereum's 11-year history have brought as much change, from leadership shakeups at the Ethereum Foundation to institutional adoption, as the past year has.
items.author: Margaux Nijkerk

items.headline: Why Aave proposes quitting 6 blockchains that earn under $5,000 a quarter
items.subheadline: A governance proposal would shut deployments on Sonic, Scroll, zkSync, Metis, Soneium and Aptos, and retire 50 asset markets elsewhere. Deposits on some have fallen more than 90%.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Major bitcoin wallet flaw drains 594 BTC in 25-minute sweep
items.subheadline: A hardware wallet randomness bug turned “impossible to guess” seeds into guessable ones, and $38 million is already gone.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: The Clarity Act isn't a ticket to sanctions evasion, actually
items.subheadline: The bill, as currently drafted, has the power to stop sanctions evasion at scale, argues Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs.
items.author: Ari Redbord

items.headline: The privacy paradox of protecting kids online
items.subheadline: We don’t need to imagine the privacy pitfalls of age verification. They’ve been happening for years, argues Cardano Foundation CEO Frederik Gregaard.
items.author: Frederik Gregaard

items.headline: The Clarity Act is the most important consumer protection effort in years
items.subheadline: Consumers should not have to wait for another crisis to get the protections they deserve, argues Summer Mersinger, CEO of the Blockchain Association.
items.author: Summer Mersinger

items.headline: AI is destroying the internet. Math is our only hope.
items.subheadline: The rise of autonomous AI agents necessitates the utilization of zero-knowledge proofs, argues Brian Trunzo, chief growth officer at Succinct Labs.
items.author: Brian Trunzo

items.headline: The KIDS Act is way worse than digital carding — it is a mass surveillance system
items.subheadline: The fact that lawmakers are even contemplating a bill that would create a surveillance and censorship regime should be a wake-up call for everyone who values privacy and free expression, argues Electronic Frontier Foundation's India McKinney.
items.author: India McKinney

items.headline: Democratizing weather derivatives through tokenization could be blockchain industry’s most important real-world use case
items.subheadline: Main Street, which faces the most significant climate-related financial risk, currently lacks an avenue to hedge weather-related risks, argues CoinDesk’s Omkar Godbole.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: SpaceX is a battleground Solana must win
items.subheadline: Perps are a trojan horse to bring all of traditional finance onchain, argues Brian Smith, president of the Jito Foundation.
items.author: Brian Smith

items.headline: Russia charges Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorism
items.subheadline: The charges could result in life imprisonment, escalating an investigation that has already led to over 100 million rubles in fines for the platform this year.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Senators ready to send stricter ethics rules on Trump's crypto ventures to White House, sources say
items.subheadline: Insiders say that the bipartisan Senate duo revamping the bill's Trump-approved ethics section have come up with something they hope wins sufficient yes votes.
items.author: Jesse Hamilton

items.headline: Founder of Russia's largest crypto mining operation transferred to a detention center
items.subheadline: Stanford University MBA graduate Igor Runets faces tax evasion and fraud charges in Russia.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: South Korea plans to tax crypto gains over $1,740 as political battle moves to parliament
items.subheadline: The country plans on taxing cryptocurrency gains from Jan. 1, 2027, signaling that it does not intend to postpone the measure for a fourth time.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Pavel Durov's Telegram messaging app faces new terror charges. Now in Australia.
items.subheadline: Australian authorities accused Telegram of allegedly failing to remove terror-related content, including a video of New Zealand's March 2019 Christchurch shooting.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: JPMorgan warns crypto risks losing out as Clarity Act stalls
items.subheadline: The bank said deteriorating prospects for U.S. market structure legislation remove a key catalyst for digital assets, even as tokenization and institutional adoption advance.
items.author: Will Canny

items.headline: There is a hidden tax risk of crypto perps that no one is talking about, says CME's CEO
items.subheadline: CME CEO Terry Duffy said a court battle over whether perpetual futures are swaps or futures could eventually affect how the IRS taxes the contracts. Independent legal experts say the issue remains unresolved.
items.author: Aoyon Ashraf

items.headline: STS Digital CEO sees three major headwinds for crypto markets
items.subheadline: Institutional options selling, AI and delayed U.S. crypto regulation are weighing on bitcoin, according to STS Digital CEO Maxime Seiler.
items.author: Will Canny

items.headline: Quantum computing nears commercial breakthrough, IBM CEO says
items.subheadline: Arvind Krishna said quantum computing will begin generating meaningful revenue before the decade ends as investment in the sector accelerates, in an interview on CNBC.
items.author: Helene Braun

items.headline: Coldcard exploit reignites Bitcoin self-custody debate after $38 million theft
items.subheadline: A software bug in popular hardware wallet Coldcard that led to the theft to this point of nearly 600 bitcoin worth roughly $38 million is prompting questions about security and whether managing private keys has become too risky for everyday investors.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: The good and the bad of perps, according to crypto traders
items.subheadline: Both retail and institutional traders worry about the funding rate.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: Tether clears $1.5 billion in profit as its safety cushion shrinks by half
items.subheadline: The stablecoin issuer stockpiled 14 tons of gold and 1,800 bitcoin, but a market slump dragged down the overall dollar value of its balance sheet.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Bitcoin (BTC) price's July gain survives hawkish Fed, AI meltdown and Coldcard fallout
items.subheadline: Bitcoin shrugged off a barrage of bad news this month, but traders remain cautious as rate hike fears and jobs data loom.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: How bitcoin cold wallets lost $70 million in an attack that never touched the devices
items.subheadline: Galaxy Research said weak seed generation let an attacker recreate likely private keys offline, sweep more than 1,000 BTC from nearly 1,200 wallets and continue searching without ever accessing the devices.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Ripple news: XRP Ledger upgrade brings back features once pulled over critical bugs
items.subheadline: The xrpld 3.3.0 release is expected next week with five proposed amendments, including two revised features that were previously withdrawn after researchers found bugs that could have allowed unauthorized transactions or fee draining.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: CZ calls for wallet diversification after $70 million Coldcard exploit
items.subheadline: After a $70 million hardware wallet drain, the Binance founder says nothing is completely safe and recommends splitting funds.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: Solana (SOL) news: Foundation's new CISO warns AI is making crypto scams more convincing
items.subheadline: Michael Coates, the foundation’s new CISO, said that AI vulnerabilities and fake identities will drive the next wave of blockchain security concerns.
items.author: Margaux Nijkerk

items.headline: SEC to review Nasdaq bitcoin options approval after CME challenge
items.subheadline: CME argues that because bitcoin is a commodity, options tied to its value fall under CFTC jurisdiction, not the SEC's authority.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Bank of Italy research suggests stablecoins aren't necessarily cheaper for remittances
items.subheadline: A Bank of Italy study found stablecoin remittances aren't systematically cheaper than traditional money transfers, with fiat on- and off-ramps accounting for most of the cost.
items.author: Jamie Crawley

items.headline: Tokenized stock trading surged 288% in July, but one QQQ token drove most of it
items.subheadline: Without that QQQ token, July volume for tokenized equities would be roughly $2.03 billion, about 30% below June’s total.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Bitcoin cold-wallet attack spreads to 4,500 addresses as losses near $89 million
items.subheadline: Galaxy Research flagged a third wave of sweeps tied to weak Coldcard-generated keys, with the attacker now targeting smaller balances and changing how funds are collected onchain.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Strategy (MSTR) news: Michael Saylor and team maintain 12% dividend for STRC
items.subheadline: Customarily, Michael Saylor and team have lifted the STRC dividend when it trades sizably below par, but not this month.
items.author: Stephen Alpher
